title: Participle adjectives (-ing and -ed)
summary: Прилагательные от причастий: **-ing** описывает то, что вызывает эмоцию (причину), **-ed** — того, кто её испытывает; плюс составные прилагательные вроде **well-known**, **time-consuming**.
ru:
## Базовое различие — и где оно ломается
Вы уже знаете: **-ing** — то, что вызывает чувство, **-ed** — тот, кто его чувствует. Для продвинутого уровня важнее тонкости, на которых ошибаются даже уверенные ученики.
> The presentation was **confusing**, so most of us left **confused**. — Презентация была запутанной, и большинство ушло в замешательстве.
> a **frightening** film / a **frightened** child — страшный фильм / испуганный ребёнок

## Один и тот же человек: -ing про характер, -ed про состояние
Про человека **-ing** описывает его свойство как «источника» эффекта, а **-ed** — его собственное состояние. Это разные утверждения.
> He is **boring**. — Он скучный (человек, с которым скучно).
> He is **bored**. — Ему скучно (сейчас).
> She is **charming** and **amusing**. — Она обаятельная и забавная.
> Don't be so **embarrassing**! — Не позорь меня!
> I felt **embarrassed**. — Мне было неловко.
- ~~I am very boring at this lecture.~~ → I am very **bored** at this lecture.
- ~~The results were disappointed.~~ → The results were **disappointing**.

## Причастие как определение после существительного
Причастие, у которого есть пояснительные слова, часто стоит **после** существительного и работает как сокращённое придаточное. Одиночное причастие обычно стоит перед ним, но некоторые (*involved, concerned*, а также причастия после *anyone, those*) стоят после существительного и в одиночку.
> The people **involved** were questioned. — Опросили причастных людей.
> Anyone **interested** should email us. — Всем заинтересованным: пишите нам.
> A **worried** parent called. — Позвонил встревоженный родитель.

## Составные прилагательные
Причастие часто образует прилагательное в паре с наречием или существительным; такие слова пишут через дефис **перед** существительным.
> a **well-known** economist — хорошо известный экономист
> a **time-consuming** process — трудоёмкий процесс
> a **fast-growing** industry — быстрорастущая отрасль
> **home-made** jam, an **awe-inspiring** view, a **long-lasting** effect
> The economist is well known. (после глагола дефис обычно не нужен)

## Усиление и предлоги
Градуальные причастные прилагательные усиливаем словами **very, extremely, deeply, rather, really**. Но **absolutely** и **utterly** с ними сочетаются только в значении полного состояния: *absolutely exhausted*, *absolutely terrifying*. Предлоги после -ed: **interested in, bored with/of, worried about, shocked by/at, tired of, surprised at/by, satisfied with**.
> I was **deeply moved** by her honesty. — Меня глубоко тронула её честность.
> We were **rather alarmed** at the news. — Новость нас довольно встревожила.

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~It was a very tired journey.~~ → It was a very **tiring** journey. (но: I was **tired** after the journey)
- ~~She seems interesting in physics.~~ → She seems **interested** in physics.
- ~~a well-knowing author~~ → a **well-known** author
en:
## The basic contrast, and its limits
You already know that **-ing** describes what causes a feeling and **-ed** describes the person who has it. At this level the details matter more.
> The presentation was **confusing**, so most of us left **confused**.
> a **frightening** film / a **frightened** child

## The same person: -ing for character, -ed for state
With people, **-ing** says what someone is like for others, while **-ed** says how they feel.
> He is **boring**. (He makes others feel bored.)
> He is **bored**. (He feels bored right now.)
> She is **charming** and **amusing**.
> Don't be so **embarrassing**! / I felt **embarrassed**.
- ~~I am very boring at this lecture.~~ → I am very **bored** at this lecture.
- ~~The results were disappointed.~~ → The results were **disappointing**.

## Participles after the noun
A participle with extra words often follows the noun, like a reduced relative clause. A single participle normally comes before it, but some (*involved, concerned*, and participles after *anyone, those*) follow the noun even on their own.
> The people **involved** were questioned.
> Anyone **interested** should email us.
> A **worried** parent called.

## Compound adjectives
Participles combine with adverbs or nouns. Before a noun they are hyphenated.
> a **well-known** economist
> a **time-consuming** process
> a **fast-growing** industry
> **home-made** jam, an **awe-inspiring** view, a **long-lasting** effect
> The economist is well known. (usually no hyphen after the verb)

## Intensifiers and prepositions
We strengthen gradable participle adjectives with **very, extremely, deeply, rather, really**. **Absolutely** and **utterly** are only used with extreme meanings: *absolutely exhausted*, *absolutely terrifying*. Typical prepositions: **interested in, bored with/of, worried about, shocked by/at, tired of, surprised at/by, satisfied with**.
> I was **deeply moved** by her honesty.
> We were **rather alarmed** at the news.

## Common mistakes
- ~~It was a very tired journey.~~ → It was a very **tiring** journey. (but: I was **tired** after the journey)
- ~~She seems interesting in physics.~~ → She seems **interested** in physics.
- ~~a well-knowing author~~ → a **well-known** author
structure:
## Форма → значение
| Форма | Значение | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| **-ing** | вызывает эффект (причина) | an **exhausting** schedule |
| **-ed** | испытывает эффект (результат) | an **exhausted** nurse |
| **-ing** о человеке | свойство, влияющее на других | He is **annoying**. |
| **-ed** о человеке | его состояние | He is **annoyed**. |

## Составные прилагательные
> наречие + причастие II: **well-known**, **well-paid**, **ill-advised** (после наречий на -ly дефис обычно не ставят: a newly built hospital)
> существительное + причастие I: **time-consuming**, **awe-inspiring**, **record-breaking**
> существительное + причастие II: **home-made**, **hand-written**, **sun-dried**
> прилагательное/наречие + причастие I: **hard-working**, **long-lasting**, **fast-moving**

## Позиция
> одиночное причастие → **перед** существительным: a **worried** parent
> причастие + пояснение → **после**: the people **involved in the case**

exercises.title: -ing или -ed?
exercises.instruction: Поставьте глагол из скобок в форму **-ing** или **-ed**.
exercises.example: The film was (bore) → The film was **boring**.

items.text: The lecture was so {{boring}} that half the audience fell asleep.
I was {{astonished}} to learn that she had resigned.
It was a {{moving}} speech, and several people were in tears.
After a {{tiring}} flight we felt completely {{exhausted}}.
Her {{confused}} expression showed that she hadn't followed the instructions.
The results were rather {{disappointing}}, and the whole team looked {{disappointed}}.
It was a {{terrifying}} experience, and the passengers were {{terrified}}.

exercises.title: Составные прилагательные
exercises.instruction: Вставьте причастие, образованное от глагола в скобках.

items.text: She is a well-{{known}} author in the Baltic states.
It was a long-{{lasting}} friendship that survived many disagreements.
The firm needs a hard-{{working}} and flexible assistant.
Updating the database is a time-{{consuming}} task.
We ate home-{{made}} bread with olive oil.
The view from the summit was awe-{{inspiring}}.
It is a purpose-{{built}} hospital with modern equipment.
He applied for a well-{{paid}} position abroad.

items.q: Several ___ residents wrote to the council.
I always find these tax forms ___.
items.why: Формы вызывают путаницу: **confusing**; после find — свойство предмета.

items.q: He is a very ___ colleague — he never stops complaining.
Why are you so ___ in medieval history all of a sudden?
The employees ___ in the dispute will be interviewed.
items.why: Сотрудники, которые вовлечены (страдательное значение) — **involved** после существительного.

items.q: It was an ___ result for such a young team.

options: She is bored with her job.
She is boring with her job.
She is bore with her job.

items.why: Те, кто проявляет интерес — **interested** после anyone.

options: After the marathon I was absolutely exhausted.
After the marathon I was absolutely exhaust.
After the marathon I was absolutely exhausting.
items.why: Состояние человека — **exhausted**; absolutely подходит к крайнему значению.

options: He was shocking by the rumours.
He was shocked by the rumours.
He was shock by the rumours.

exercises.title: Перефразируйте
exercises.instruction: Перепишите предложение, начав с указанных слов и используя причастие на **-ed**.

answers: Everyone was annoyed by the delay.
Everyone was annoyed at the delay.
Everyone was annoyed about the delay.

items.prompt: The speech inspired the young graduates. → The young graduates ...
answers: The young graduates were inspired by the speech.

items.prompt: The sudden noise frightened the children. → The children ...
answers: The children were frightened by the sudden noise.
The children were frightened by the noise.

items.prompt: The documentary fascinated my father. → My father ...
answers: My father was fascinated by the documentary.
My father was fascinated with the documentary.

items.prompt: The price increase worries many shoppers. → Many shoppers ...
answers: Many shoppers are worried about the price increase.
Many shoppers are worried by the price increase.

items.prompt: The ending of the book disappointed me. → I ...
answers: I was disappointed by the ending of the book.
I was disappointed with the ending of the book.
I was disappointed at the ending of the book.
I was disappointed in the ending of the book.
I was disappointed by the book's ending.
I was disappointed with the book's ending.
It was a very tiring day.
That was a very tiring day.
It was a very exhausting day.
That was a very exhausting day.

items.prompt: Мы были очень удивлены его решением.
answers: We were very surprised by his decision.
We were very surprised at his decision.
I'm not interested in this project.
I am not interested in this project.
I'm not interested in the project.
I am not interested in the project.
I'm not interested in that project.
I am not interested in that project.

That was a thrilling game.
The results of the study didn't surprise me.

I wasn't surprised by the results of the study.
I was not surprised by the results of the study.
I wasn't surprised at the results of the study.
I was not surprised at the results of the study.

The study's results did not surprise me.

exercises.title: Напишите о себе
exercises.instruction: Ответьте полными предложениями, используя причастные прилагательные.

items.prompt: Describe the most boring or most exhausting day you have had recently.
items.sample: Last Monday was exhausting: I had three long meetings, and the last one was so boring that I could hardly stay awake.

items.prompt: What are you interested in, and what do you find fascinating about it?
items.sample: I'm interested in astronomy. I find it fascinating that the light we see left the star thousands of years ago.

items.prompt: Write about a film or book that you found surprising or disappointing.
items.sample: The last novel I read was disappointing. I was expecting a surprising ending, but everything was quite predictable.

items.prompt: Name two compound adjectives (e.g. well-known) and use each in a sentence.
items.sample: She's a well-known journalist. Preparing the report was a time-consuming job.
